items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: He was with T Holder. Oh sure, that band there is where Andy Craig slipped away from T Holder.

ctx.x: I had a whole bunch of names of people that I wanted to ask you about, that played around Texas and Kansas City and Connecticut. Did you ever think of the name of T Holder's singer? Do you know who that would have been? Featero?
He was with T Holder. Oh sure, that band there is where Andy Craig slipped away from T Holder. Oh yeah. And that's the same musicians.
Yeah, so he had played T Holder. What about A.G. Gonday's reputation? What kind of drummer was he?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: And you had Lansford, my band, Andy Craig, T Holder, Troy Floyd, Trent.

ctx.x: What bands were famous for their riffs then?

Well, most all bands. All of them set their riffs. The Blue Devils, which was Ben and Morton's band, great riff band. And of course, from there came the Count Basie band. And you had Lansford, my band, Andy Craig, T Holder, Troy Floyd, Trent. Now Trent was a little more sophisticated band, something on the P-Rong style band. Played mostly the high class hotels and schools and colleges in those days. But they also played a lot of gigs, outside gigs. It was one of these real fine, classy bands, Trent was. Troy was…
I know some of the guys that work for C.G. Khan, and maybe we should ask them.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: the other trumpet player I'm referring to in the Southwest that was T Holder

ctx.x: That's how I remember him. Yeah. Well now, Tommy Howell played with Sonny Clapp. He played a little like Biderback.
That's right. No, Biderback's a trumpet player. Now the other fellow, the other trumpet player I'm referring to in the Southwest that was T Holder. What? T Holder.
